definition: A set of coordinate axes with an origin, together with clocks, that an observer uses to give the position and time of events.
A reference frame that is not accelerating, so Newton's first law holds in it; any frame moving at constant velocity relative to it is also inertial.
The principle that Newton's laws of motion are the same in every inertial reference frame, with events and velocities converted between frames by $x' = x - vt$, $t' = t$ and $u' = u - v$.
